title: Should you hand-code the items the coder called positive, or sample the audit by the coder's label?
summary: On 3,188 real GoEmotions comments, four automated coders (three cut-offs of a naive-Bayes classifier and a word list; not LLMs) and a hand-coded audit of 50 to 800 items, sampling the audit by the coder's own label barely helped, and auditing only the coder's positives was badly wrong. The prediction-powered interval from a random audit was about 23% wider than the same kind of sample read as stratified by coder label (mean width 0.201 against 0.163 at 100 items), a property of the interval formula rather than of the draw; equal numbers per coder label were 9% wider than that, and oracle Neyman allocation 1–2% narrower. The sensitivity-style audit (hand-code only coder-positive items, assume the rest hold no positives) gave intervals a quarter as wide with coverage 0.000 in all 20 coder-and-size cells, because the coders missed 12–16% of the corpus's positives (bias −0.117 to −0.160 on a true 0.247); it can only estimate the coder's precision. One code, one corpus, one split; standard errors ignore the finite-population correction.
lede: should you hand-code only what the coder called positive, or sample the audit by the coder's label? On 3,188 GoEmotions comments, a positives-only audit had 0 of 1,000 intervals covering the truth for every coder (it misses the coder's false negatives); stratifying by label barely helped. Not an LLM; one corpus.
